content: The reviewers independently assessed the studies. There were no clear methods to minimize errors during data extraction. The methods used to combine studies were appropriate. The likelihood of publication bias was not assessed. Recommendations for policy and/or practice were supported by the reported data. The specific directives for new research were unclear. The overall critical appraisal score for this section was low, with a score of 2 out of 11. For randomized controlled trials (RCTs), true randomization was used for assigning participants to treatment groups. Allocation to treatment groups was not concealed. Treatment groups were similar at baseline. Participants and those delivering treatment were not blinded to treatment assignment, as these items were not applicable. Outcome assessors were not blinded to treatment assignment. Treatment groups were treated identically except for the intervention of interest. Follow-up was complete, and differences between groups in terms of follow-up were adequately described and analyzed. Participants were analyzed in the groups to which they were randomized, though this was unclear in some cases. Outcomes were measured in the same way for treatment groups and were measured reliably. Appropriate statistical analysis was used. The trial design was appropriate, and any deviations from the standard RCT design were accounted for in the conduct and analysis of the trial. The overall critical appraisal score for RCTs was high, with a score of 9 out of 11. For pre-post studies, there was no confusion about the sequence of variables. Participants included in comparisons were not similar, and there was no control group. Multiple measurements of the outcome were not consistently performed preand post-intervention. Follow-up was incomplete in some cases, and differences between groups in terms of follow-up were not always adequately described and analyzed. Outcomes of participants included in comparisons were not consistently measured in the same way. Outcomes were measured reliably in some studies but were unclear in others. Appropriate statistical analysis was used in most cases. The overall critical appraisal score for pre-post studies was low to moderate, with scores ranging from 2 to 5 out of 6. For cross-sectional studies, the criteria for inclusion in the sample were clearly defined. Study subjects and settings were described in detail. The exposure was not measured in a valid and reliable way, and objective, standard criteria were not used for measurement of the condition. Confounding factors were not identified, and strategies to address confounding factors were not stated. Outcomes were not consistently measured in a valid and reliable way. Appropriate statistical analysis was used. The overall critical appraisal score for cross-sectional studies was moderate, with scores of 3 out of 6. For qualitative studies, there was congruity between the stated philosophical perspective and the research methodology, as well as between the research methodology and the research question, data collection methods, data representation and analysis, and interpretation of results. There was no statement locating the researcher culturally or theoretically, and the influence of the researcher on the research and vice versa was not addressed. Participants and their voices were adequately represented. The research was ethical, with evidence of ethical approval by an appropriate body. Conclusions drawn in the research report flowed from the analysis or interpretation of the data.
